straight down hill and across Kushk valley to west bank
up the course of the Kushk to the next demarcated pillar
completed description and 1887 protocol; intermediate terrain controls/posts must be retained during digitization
straight to point on Murghab above Yaki-Yuz/Yaki-Yangi canal head
synopsis accepted as definitive by the 1887 protocol; exact post sequence remains a digitization dependency

existing Bosagha–Khamiab local frontier retained subject to canal/land reservations specified by the protocol

geometry.derivationNote: The line is now encoded as a source-derived sequence of segment semantics rather than an undifferentiated pending line. The official texts prove where the frontier is straight, follows ridge/watershed, follows a river course/thalweg, or relies on mapped/local-demarcation controls. This still does not justify a geometry-verified full polyline: mapped points A-D, the complete 1-19/36-66 pillar synopsis, the later eastern posts and terrain-following vertices must be digitized from the authoritative maps/descriptions before coordinate geometry is promoted.

territoryChanges.notes: This record is the documentary completion/demarcation event and therefore does not itself add or remove territory-area geometry in replay. The seven explicitly coordinate-defined controls remain the separate geometry-verified spatial subset; full boundary-line digitization remains a boundary-overlay task rather than an area mutation.

geometry.derivationNote: Seven trigonometric/pillar controls are explicitly coordinate-defined in the 1887 protocol and cross-checked against the parallel Russian official publication. They are rendered as MultiPoint only. Activation is conservatively delayed to the 26 January 1888 completion of the commission work; the controls themselves were defined earlier.
